scope: Recompute only existing national NCHS 2003–2006 age-count aggregates and inspect frozen observer/first-birth equations. No new microdata extraction, household/equilibrium solves, rescoring or adoption.
measurement_findings: The 25.976 grouped mean is reproduced exactly from existing counts.
The 25.161 raw mean records completed integer ages; adding 0.5 gives a 25.661 proxy under a uniform-within-single-year approximation, not an observed continuous-age mean.
Common four-year grouping is a measurement choice; collapsing births below18/above45 is a separate support assumption.
Age30 is a model-cell boundary; the observed 30+ share still includes outside-model-support births in its denominator.
Reproduction establishes arithmetic, not population equivalence or structural identification.
identification_findings: Current retrieved reviews explicitly do not establish structural identification. More moments than free parameters is necessary but insufficient.
First-birth attempt probability has index pi_a*(DeltaV-xi)/kappa_1; DeltaV depends on the rest of the model and continuation values. Cost and scale can partly substitute in aggregate moments.
The common-scale restriction kappa_1=kappa_C is distinct from removing xi. Both remain deferred simplification checks.

A local sensitivity assessment should renormalize psi consistently with the2.10 normalization, inspect distinct moment responses and account for other jointly estimated parameters. No such new calculation is run here.

slide_core_lead_check.finding: Core first-birth success-branch cost, first/later taste scales and logistic attempt formula match the inspected sequential code. This is not a full slide certification; shock-location convention and experimental versus reference restrictions require separate care.

next_decision: Retain the proposed fertility outcomes for review while explicitly deciding support/age measurement and establishing the evidence needed for separate parameter identification.
